Subject: Hyperlane POC — request for architecture + throughput gating

Rachel — thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re kicking off the internal prep for the POC and want to lock down two things before we hand this to our SREs:

1) An architecture deep-dive so our infra team understands how Redwood will fit into our VPC and what KV/prefix caching looks like.
2) A short, tightly scoped throughput run to validate token targets (aiming for ~8M tokens/hour steady-state, burst to 12M).

Can we schedule a 90-minute session that splits 45/45: arch + live throughput run? Our ideal window is Tue 2026-10-06 10:00–11:30 PDT but we can be flexible if needed. Also: can you share a brief list of prerequisites (agent versions, expected artifacts, and any runbook)?

Thanks — Samir

Quick technical note — if Hyperlane is running the traffic from a VPC, we need:
- SSH access to the jump-box (user/key) and one test dataset mounted (we prefer a 10K-turn prompt set)
- Model binary/tag they plan to exercise (we support the 7B/13B families; if they want quantized 8-bit variants, we need to pre-warm kernels)
- Network perf check (iperf/mtr) between test host and our collector host; aim for <30ms RTT and >1.5Gbps baseline for stable numbers

For the load run: I suggest a two-phase burn: 20-minute ramp to 8M tokens/hr, 30-minute steady, then 10-minute 12M burst. That gives us enough time to capture KV/cache behavior. I’ll prepare load-config-v2.yaml and the token-targets.xlsx and drop them to Rachel for Hyperlane.

— Irene
